title: Subtree Removal Game with Fibonacci Tree
summary: A Fibonacci tree is constructed using the order function where order(0) is empty, order(1) is a single node, and order(n) is a root with the left subtree as order(n-2) and the right as order(n-1).
statement: A Fibonacci tree is constructed using the order function where order(0) is empty, order(1) is a single node, and order(n) is a root with the left subtree as order(n-2) and the right as order(n-1). Alice and Bob play a game starting with Alice, removing a node and its subtree per turn, with the loser being the one who deletes the root. Given n, determine if Alice wins optimally, with both players playing perfectly, and a subtree being a node and all its descendants including the node itself.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100; order zero is empty and order one is a single node.
Order n has children of orders n-2 and n-1; a move removes a chosen node and its subtree.
The player forced to delete the root loses; return whether Alice wins with optimal play.
hints: Treat deleting the protected root as the losing forced action, so legal play ends when no child component remains.
A removable rooted component has value one plus the xor of its child components; the protected root exposes only the xor.
Let c0=0,c1=1 and c[n]=(c[n-2] xor c[n-1])+1; its zero protected values occur exactly when n mod 6 is one.
The component recurrence follows the green-tree pruning mex rule. Its six-step invariant proves precisely those orders are losing.
editorial: The component recurrence follows the green-tree pruning mex rule. Its six-step invariant proves precisely those orders are losing.

tests.explanation: The protected-root position has nonzero nim value, so Alice can leave Bob the losing state.
There is no legal non-root removal, so Alice must delete the root and loses.
